baseline: Existing TechDev Copper/Gold use remains unchanged; this task is decomposition research only.
decision_divergence: Useful only if decomposition changes confidence in, scope of, or horizon interpretation of the existing Copper/Gold evidence; explanatory arithmetic alone is insufficient.
falsifier: Independent data fail to reproduce the claimed horizon-dependent attribution, attribution is unstable across reasonable anchors, or decomposition adds no decision-relevant distinction.
hypothesis: Copper may dominate higher-frequency variance while gold may dominate slow drift; the claim must be independently reproduced and may fail.
instructions: Treat all numeric claims supplied by Claude or prior models as unverified until independently reproduced.
Use exact instrument identities, frequencies, anchor dates and source provenance.
Separate drift attribution from variance attribution.
Do not run a halving-clock ablation in the same experiment.
Do not create a threshold, sensor, weight, market state or portfolio action.
kill_condition: Close as explanatory-only if stable incremental value cannot be demonstrated; do not modify the existing TechDev signal on that basis.
primary_goal: Independently test whether Copper/Gold interpretation changes when movement, variance and slow MACD-style drift are decomposed by numerator and denominator rather than described from endpoint moves.
question: How much of Copper/Gold movement and slow-signal drift is attributable to copper versus gold across fixed, reproducible horizons, and does attribution materially change with horizon?
required_evidence: independently sourced copper series with exact instrument identity and timestamps
independently sourced gold series with exact instrument identity and timestamps
fixed anchor dates declared before calculation
source hashes or reproducible source receipts
short versus weekly versus slow 2M signal attribution
title: Copper/Gold Driver Decomposition by Horizon
